description: Estamos desarrollando Red Frontier: Mars Mission, un videojuego educativo sobre la supervivencia y la exploración en Marte. Nos interesan la programación, el diseño 3D y la ciencia espacial. Ya tenemos una campaña 2D jugable y estamos llevando sus misiones a Unity para que puedas recorrer la base, reparar paneles solares, cultivar alimentos y analizar las muestras que trae el rover.
summary: Red Frontier: Mars Mission is a playable 3D educational game that lets students manage a Martian outpost and experience the engineering trade-offs behind survival. Players balance oxygen, energy, water, food and materials while caring for the crew. They explore the base in first person, construct facilities and complete hands-on station tasks with tools. Rover expeditions return samples for laboratory analysis, while three campaigns introduce essential systems, environmental emergencies and scientific exploration. A science archive links game mechanics to NASA resources and distinguishes observed mission evidence from simplified game rules. The browser game offers desktop and touch controls, English by default and Spanish in settings. Our goal is to make resource dependencies and the consequences of mission decisions understandable through play.
details:
PROJECT AND CHALLENGE

Red Frontier: Mars Mission addresses Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer by making students responsible for a Martian outpost. The player must decide which systems to build, which equipment to maintain and how to use limited materials and crew work shifts. These choices affect the settlement rather than remaining abstract menu decisions.

HOW IT WORKS

The game combines resource management with a first-person 3D environment. Players inspect objectives, move through the base, equip a scanner, hammer, medkit or container, and hold the action to perform station work. Releasing the action interrupts the task. The eight station types cover habitat care, oxygen production, water recovery, food production, workshop maintenance, solar power, laboratory analysis and communications. Structures can be built and upgraded. Automated crew assistance can contribute to construction and station work.

Rover expeditions consume battery power and involve route choices. Returned samples must be collected and analysed before contributing to science objectives. Three campaigns unlock in sequence: First Landing introduces essential systems, Survival Protocol adds environmental crises and repair priorities, and Beyond the Horizon emphasizes exploration and scientific progress. Dust storms, equipment faults and other events create competing demands.

NASA RESOURCES AND SCIENTIFIC BOUNDARIES

The science archive separates mission observations, scientific interpretation and the game simplification. MOXIE informs the oxygen-production concept. Other cards cite Curiosity radiation observations, InSight weather, dust effects on Opportunity, subsurface ice research, Perseverance science and Mars solar conjunction. The game also offers searches of the NASA Image and Video Library. The starry background uses NASA/Goddard Deep Star Maps 2020, with ESA/Gaia/DPAC credits. Gameplay rates and timescales are educational parameters. The terrain, Olympus Mons scale and celestial placement include artistic choices and do not constitute a navigational or operational mission model.

TECHNOLOGY AND ACCESS

The browser game uses TypeScript, Three.js, React and WebGL, with Blender assets and compressed models and textures. It preserves the resource, construction and campaign rules developed for the earlier 2D version. English is the initial language and Spanish is available in settings. Keyboard/mouse and touch controls, graphics settings and local browser saves support access on different devices. The current game is playable; visual polish, performance on physical phones and learning outcomes still need further evaluation.

INTENDED IMPACT

We want students to explain why a base needs interdependent systems and to reason about the consequences of a mission plan. Practice connects resource feedback with direct work at the station. These are intended learning benefits, not measured educational results.

AI ASSISTANCE AND VISUAL DISCLOSURE

ChatGPT/Codex assisted code development, debugging and presentation preparation. Image-generation tools contributed illustrative game artwork. Three real game screenshots in the linked demo were retouched with image_gen to improve presentation lighting and clarity, and carry the visible label AI-retouched game capture. They are promotional retouches rather than evidence of changes to the playable renderer. The credited MOXIE photograph is an unmodified NASA/JPL-Caltech source image.

DEMO AND REFERENCES

The demo is a seven-slide English presentation. The game and demo links require no account. Detailed source credits, external tools and the AI disclosure are available at https://red-frontier-3d.pages.dev/submission-sources.html .
